description:
RefCell borrows are released by copying or by hand-placed drops.

Evidence (develop @ cca160808):
- src/compiler2/source.rs:965-987 struct_layout clones the whole schema
  (`schemas_registry().borrow().get(schema_id).clone()`) to release the
  registry borrow, then copies the identity and offsets into StructLayout.
  StructLayout is already the owned extract; building it inside the borrow
  needs no schema clone. The doc comment explaining the clone goes with it.
- src/compiler2/drive_harness.rs:795-798 defined_names collects the ids to
  drop the borrow, then re-borrows once per id through qualified_name.
- src/telemetry/jsonl.rs:1108, :1113, :1122, :1133 four `drop(canon)`
  before self.append / self.append_without_world.
- src/compiler2/pull.rs:2286 (and pull/rooted.rs:668)
  `let external = self.session.external.clone()` -- an Rc cloned to hold a
  borrow of session.external while session.memo is mutated.
- src/compiler2/jobs/body.rs:1695-1698 `let result = ..; drop(sources);
  result`.

Before building, per site: establish what the released borrow would
otherwise collide with (does JsonlBackend::append touch `canon`? does the
pull path call a &mut self method while `external` is borrowed?). A site
whose drop or clone is load-bearing is recorded here with the reason and
left; a site that is not is restructured so the borrow's scope is the
block's scope.

Depends on .3, which settles the lend / take idiom for cells.

Removal ledger: the schema clone and its comment; each drop/clone shown
not to be load-bearing.

Signal: gate green, no golden/census/pin movement.
title: A RefCell borrow ends where its block ends
